claims.speaker: Chris Wright, U.S. Energy Secretary
claims.quote: Nearly 9 million barrels per day leaving through Hormuz, as a seven-day average.
claims.note: Also reported by Reuters commentary of 2026-08-24.

claims.speaker: Chris Wright, U.S. Energy Secretary
claims.quote: About 15 million barrels per day of total regional flow: roughly 9 through Hormuz plus 5-7 via bypass pipelines and export routes.
claims.note: Not a Hormuz-only figure; includes bypass routes.

claims.speaker: U.S. administration
claims.quote: A claimed 15 million barrels moved on one particular day.
claims.note: Exceptional single-day volume claim, not an average rate.

claims.speaker: U.S. officials
claims.quote: About 10 million barrels per day exiting via the strait itself.
claims.note: Axios described this as roughly half of prewar Hormuz volume.

claims.speaker: U.S. officials
claims.quote: 15 to 20 tankers entering and exiting each night in the U.S.-protected corridor.
claims.note: Inbound plus outbound combined; not equivalent to loaded outbound tankers.

claims.speaker: Chris Wright, U.S. Energy Secretary
claims.quote: An average of about 8 million barrels of oil per day had left Hormuz over the prior seven days.
claims.note: Later reading of the same seven-day series as c1; different windows, not a correction.

estimates.note: Range across commercial trackers; Persian Gulf loadings and subsequent deliveries not corroborating the full U.S. figure.
Estimate explicitly attempts to include dark transits and ship-to-ship transfers.

scope_definitions.hormuz_outbound: Oil claimed or estimated to be exiting through the Strait of Hormuz itself.
scope_definitions.regional_total_including_bypass: Hormuz flow plus bypass pipelines and export routes; not comparable to Hormuz-only figures.
scope_definitions.ship_transits_in_and_out: Vessel transits counted in both directions; includes empty inbound ships, so not a loaded-outbound count.

method.gap: The verification gap is the claimed flow minus the independent tracker consensus, computed only within one scope, one unit, and one time window. It is labeled unverified, not false.
method.estimates_provenance: Independent tracker figures reach this dataset secondhand, as reported by the named press outlet on each row.
method.resolution: The gap can only be resolved retrospectively: Gulf loadings, destination arrivals and official trade data. First referee: official Iraq/Kuwait/Saudi export figures for August 2026, expected around October-November 2026, already tracked by this site's official-tally instrument.
method.dark_transits: Ships operating without AIS may explain part of the gap (a tracker undercount). A missed VLCC is roughly 2 million barrels. The explanation cuts both ways and is not adjudicated here.

guardrails: The difference is labeled unverified, never lying or exaggeration.
Comparisons never cross scopes or units.
Anonymous attributions are marked as such.
PortWatch activity indices are never converted into barrels-per-day estimates.
Every value carries a dated, linked source.
